items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: I walked in there one night and Sammy Margolis was sitting at the bar and he says, “You playing drums on this job, Jake?” I says, “Yeah, I am, Sammy.”

ctx.x: Was that a particularly significant gig for you?

Yeah, yeah. It was so good I was walking to work one night, I’d been in there with Anita O’Day, I’d been there with the Hi Lo’s, I’d been there with Lambert, Hendricks & Ross, you name it. I was there with these people [inaudible]. I walked in there one night and Sammy Margolis was sitting at the bar and he says, “You playing drums on this job, Jake?” I says, “Yeah, I am, Sammy.” “It’s going to change your life.” I says, “You think so?” He says, “Yeah. It’ll shoot you off in another direction. You’ll never play…

oh, this is how it’s supposed to go. Everybody’s supposed to contribute. Not like that battling and battling of Maynard, you know, and guys run up and down, trombones and all that, oof, Jesus. Yeah, this was great.
